study.question: Can auxiliary residual capacity be removed from the 14/10 incumbent while preserving click AUC and reducing measured prediction cost, and does further click-directed allocation help at a fixed total residual width?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: g2-r0029-joint_allocation_click14 reaches validation click AUC0.6671249391761293 versus0.6669688107018676 for uniform11/11 at the same32108245 parameters, but inference26.7804s versus25.5117s and p50/p95=16.1581/16.3692ms versus15.9865/16.0624ms establish no cost improvement. At budget32, click11/aux7 has AUC0.6667125463092708 versus0.6665364836641035 for uniform8/8 at32095333 parameters; again no demonstrated latency improvement. These single-seed directions suggest testing whether retaining click width14 while reducing each auxiliary from10 to6 preserves quality better than reducing click to11. Counterevidence is substantial: embedding12 and scorer-half lose AUC; uniform residual8 loses quality against the current incumbent; fewer residual parameters have not yielded reliable prediction savings. Proposed mechanism is marginal task-specific bottleneck utility, not a new architecture. Auxiliary context gradients may make auxiliary capacity consequential for click. This remains a hypothesis, not established transfer or mechanism support.

study.proposed_difference: Four standalone cells form a 2x2 design in total residual hidden-width budget S in{44,32} and click-minus-each-auxiliary gap d in{4,8}: click=(S+3d)/4, auxiliary=(S-d)/4. Reference(S44,d4)=14/10; small bridge(S32,d4)=11/7; new auxiliary reduction(S32,d8)=14/6; new matched-budget reallocation(S44,d8)=17/9. Only CONFIG values and matching constructor defaults change. All learned dimensions outside the residual bank remain fixed. Each hidden unit costs analytically1076 parameters, inferred from host-measured prior counts: total/dense/embedding are32108245/315029/31793216 atS44 and32095333/302117/31793216 atS32. The12912-parameter reduction is4.10% of dense parameters but only0.0402% of total; latency improvement is explicitly uncertain. Re-run both archived cells as byte-identical consistency bridges, not independent replications.
predictions: Predeclare current-incumbent preservation tolerance0.0002 absolute click AUC for this prospective round: a useful candidate must reach at least0.6669249391761293 and be no more than0.0002 below the contemporaneous14/10 bridge. This is a screening tolerance, not a statistical noninferiority conclusion. It also exceeds the original frozen joint best AUC0.666753547526167. Do not retroactively relabel earlier outcomes under this new round criterion.

AtS32,14/6 should outperform11/7 if click capacity is more valuable on the margin; atS44,17/9 should outperform14/10 if that allocation trend persists. Gains at both budgets provide stronger controlled support than a single winning cell. Examine the allocation interaction [AUC17/9-AUC14/10]-[AUC14/6-AUC11/7] without interpreting one seed as significance.

Direct auxiliary removal14/10->14/6 should preserve click AUC while reducing total parameters by12912. Utility additionally requires at least3% lower full-validation inference_seconds AND model-only batch p50, with p95 no more than1% worse, relative to the same-round14/10 control under identical hardware, batch order, timing definitions and loading. Report train_seconds, peak memory, throughput and all task metrics even if speed fails. Parameter savings alone do not meet utility.

Bridge AUCs should match their archived receipts within1e-6 absolute, with exact source/config/parameter identity. A same-seed bridge is execution consistency evidence only. All four tasks must remain finite with[B,1] outputs. Report auxiliary mean AUC separately: a drop greater than0.01 versus the same-round reference marks a multitask tradeoff and excludes a joint-preservation claim, even if click/cost passes.

The two cells at eachS have exactly equal analytical parameter counts. Cost and quality changes within each budget therefore test allocation rather than parameter count; actual operation timing may still vary with width.
falsifiers: 14/6 fails the fixed AUC threshold or same-round tolerance, or shows no measured prediction-cost reduction: reject its practical utility under this protocol. AUC preservation without speedup is a capacity-tolerance result only.

17/9 fails to beat14/10 at fixedS44, and14/6 fails to beat11/7 at fixedS32: no support for further click-directed allocation over the tested range. Mixed signs imply budget-dependent or noisy allocation, not a general rule.

If only one budget supports allocation, or effects fail in later paired seeds/user-cluster uncertainty analyses, retain provisional evidence and withdraw a robust mechanism claim. One failed width does not prove all auxiliary capacity necessary.

Any bridge mismatch beyond1e-6 AUC, incorrect counts, masks, task order, gradient ownership or nonfinite outputs invalidates attribution until diagnosed. Retain failures and costs; do not adjust data, scoring or frozen recipe.
No claimed speedup survives matched timing repetition, or p95/auxiliary tradeoff guardrails fail: retain the measured quality/cost outcome and do not promote a joint efficient model.

cost_plan.stop_rule: This proposal contains exactly four variants. Do not change the hard deadline or per-trial cap. Stop before launching work that cannot fit the full authorized unit and remaining reserves. On a bridge discrepancy or boundary failure, retain receipts and diagnose rather than interpret effects. After host feedback, stop width-only efficiency screening if neither new candidate meets both quality and speed gates; a quality-only win is not scientific efficiency success. A single run may nominate a candidate, but confirm a speed claim with at least three matched timing measurements where the host supports them, preserving all charges. If repetition is unavailable, label speed provisional. Choose among candidates passing gates by lowest inference_seconds, resolving differences under1% by click AUC; use no auxiliary mean for primary ranking.
